newsitem.title: USA: Valero profits hurt by natgas price drop.
newsitem.headline: Valero profits hurt by natgas price drop.

text.p: Valero Energy Corp Thursday reported a decline in first quarter net income citing a drop in operating income from natural gas operations which was partially offset by lower refinery feedstock prices.
Profits delined to $15.4 million, or $0.29 per share, from $19.9 million, or $0.39 per share, in 1996's initial quarter.

Valero said its refining and marketing operations had record operating income of $43.5 million, compared to $15.2 million in last year's first quarterm adding the increase was due primarily to an improvement in the discount for residual fuel purchases and higher gasoline-to-crude premiums.

Operating income from the natural gas related services segment was $10.9 million in the latest quarter, down from $47.5 million in the first quarter of 1996 on lower natural gas sales prices and margins.

These resulted primarily from unusually warm winter weather in the Eastern United States in February and March, and a lower contribution from the segment's price risk management activities, Valero said.
The decrease was partially offset by improved natural gas liquids margins resulting from higher NGL product prices.
It noted NGLs were supported by strong crude oil and refined product markets and continued tight NGL inventories.

"The significant improvement in our refining and marketing segment's reported operating income demonstrates the leverage we have to improvements in residual fuel oil discounts and gasoline prices," said chief executive Bill Greehey.
"Higher crude oil prices during the first half of the quarter helped support favorable discounts for our residual fuel oil purchases.
